chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Urama, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Compete with one another in doing good deeds for your brothers, and be among its people, for Paradise has a door called 'Al-Ma'ruf' (Good Deeds), none shall enter it except the one who performed good deeds during the life of the world.'

For indeed, when a servant walks to fulfill the need of his believing brother, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assigns two angels to him, one on his right and one on his left, who seek forgiveness for him from his Lord and supplicate for the fulfillment of his need.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was more joyful with the fulfillment of a believer's need when it reached him than the needy person himself was.'

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوف: The door of Paradise named after good deeds
key_terms.قَضَاءُ الْحَاجَةِ: Fulfilling the need / Meeting the requirement

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward and angelic accompaniment for fulfilling a believer's need?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* underscores the spiritual magnitude of *qada' al-hajah* (fulfilling a believer's need) by personifying it as a specific gate to Paradise, thereby elevating social service to an act of worship. It further illustrates the divine mechanism of reward, where angels flank the believer to seek forgiveness and pray for the fulfillment of their own needs, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnectedness of the community (*ummah*) and divine mercy.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Awrama, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Compete with each other regarding the good works to your bretheren, and become from its deserving ones, for the Paradise has a Door called ‘The good works’, none shall enter it except the one who did the good works during the life of the world.

So if the servant were to walk regarding a need of his Momin brother, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Allocate two Angels to him, one on his right and the other on his left, both seeking Forgiveness for him from his Lordazwj, and both supplicating for the fulfilment of his needs’.
Then heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj! Rasool-Allahsaww was more joyful with the fulfilment of a need of the Momin when it (news) arrived to himsaww than the needy one was himself’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Uramah from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn abu Hamza from his father from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Compete in al-Ma’ruf doing good to your brothers (in belief) and be of such people; in paradise there is a door called al-Ma’ruf through which no one can enter except those who have performed al-Ma’ruf (a virtuous deed) in the worldly life.

If a servant (of Allah) walks to help his believing brother (in belief), Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, appoints two angels one from the right and one from the left to ask forgiveness for him from his Lord and pray for his wish to come true.’
The Imam then said, ‘By Allah, the Messenger of Allah becomes happier for the coming true of the wish of the needy believer than the needy believer himself.’”
